claims.text: The Zircaloy-4 substrate composition is Zr-98.2%, Sn-1.5%, Fe-0.2%, and Cr-0.1%.
The as-deposited AlTiCrZrNbTa coating is dense, defect-free, amorphous, and approximately 4 μm thick.
The proposed intervention is to use approximately 10 at.% Al in the sputtered coating while holding the other deposition parameters constant.
A coating containing approximately 10 at.% Al will form a dense, continuous composite oxide layer during high-temperature steam oxidation.
The composite oxide formed at approximately 10 at.% Al will primarily comprise Al2O3, TiO2, and Cr2O3.
The composite oxide layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The composite oxide layer helps preserve coating-to-substrate adhesion.
Al-free coatings produce fragmented oxide layers under comparable oxidation conditions.
Excessive Al promotes intermetallic phases or oxide fragmentation that compromises the protective barrier.
Favorable oxide-formation Gibbs energies promote nucleation of Al2O3 and TiO2 in the proposed optimal composition.
Chromium becomes enriched at the surface and stabilizes Cr2O3.
Al-free or low-Al coatings fail to form enough protective oxide.
The approximately 10 at.% Al coating will have a significantly lower oxidation rate than the Al-free coating.
The approximately 10 at.% Al coating will exhibit lower mass gain than the Al-free coating.
The approximately 10 at.% Al coating will exhibit less oxygen penetration and minimal interfacial oxygen content relative to the Al-free coating.
The oxide on the approximately 10 at.% Al coating will remain continuous and adherent after the specified oxidation exposure.
The Al-free coating undergoes accelerated oxidation under conditions similar to the proposed test.
The proposed enhancement should hold at 1000 °C for 60 minutes and, for the approximately 10 at.% Al coating, at 1100 °C for 30 minutes in flowing steam.
The effective Al range appears to be approximately 9–14 at.%, with approximately 10 at.% being the most effective composition.
The magnitude of the oxidation-rate improvement may vary with subtle changes in processing conditions.
